Overview
Jev in a nutshell
Jev makes the quick decisions around your AI, so the expensive model only does the work that needs it.
WHAT IT IS
A model that picks an answer from options you define, with a probability for each. It never writes prose.
WHY IT HELPS
Fast and cheap enough to run on every request: 70–500 ms and $0.042 per million input tokens.
WHERE IT FITS
The many small decisions around your AI: routing, safety checks, triage, labeling and scoring.
An LLM is the expert who writes the report. Jev is the clerk who sorts the mail in an instant.
Speed and cost figures are TypeSafe’s.

What it does
Typed decisions, not text
Send a state and some typed questions. Jev answers them all in one pass, with probabilities and a confidence value.
state
text, JSON or name and value pairs
Jev
one pass
choice
the picked option and a probability for each
score
a value on your scale, plus probabilities
noul
the probability that a statement is true
Sources: TypeSafe docs, InfoQ, LangChain
Architecture
Jev and LLMs
Illustrative. TypeSafe has not published Jev’s size, architecture details or training data; this is from its own descriptions and independent tests.
Options
Three question types
CHOICE
Pick one option
Works like a switch. Returns the choice, a probability for each option and a confidence value.
Used in scenarios 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9
NOUL
Yes or no
Works like an if. Returns a number from 0 to 1: the probability that a statement is true.
Used in scenario 2
SCORE
Rate on a scale
Rates the state on levels you describe. Returns a score, probabilities and a confidence value.
Used in scenarios 5, 6
Sources: TypeSafe docs, dsebastien.net. The scenario mapping is this deck’s suggestion.
Speed
Jev and Laya
Laya is an open-weights System One model from Convai Innovations, built by Nandakishor Mukkunnoth.
Launched around 22 September 2026, a week after Jev. Apache 2.0 licence, 421M parameters, runs on your own hardware.
32.8 ms per question against 236–276 ms for Jev: about 7.8× faster.
Ten questions: about 72 ms against about 1,500 ms.
Not like-for-like: Laya was measured locally on a Tesla T4 GPU, and the Jev figures are third-party and include the network. Sources: eesel.ai, Laya website
System 1 and System 2
Two ways of thinking
System 1
Fast, automatic and effortless. It answers before you decide to think. 2 + 2 = ? Four, instantly.
System 2
Slow, deliberate and effortful. It does the arithmetic, the checking and the planning. 17 × 24 = ? You have to work it out.
Popularised by Daniel Kahneman in Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011). He credits Keith Stanovich and Richard West for the terms.
Source: Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011); Hebrew edition shown

Math, counting, explaining itself

Scenario 1 of 9
Model routing
Send each prompt to the model that fits it, so easy requests go to a small, cheap LLM and only hard ones reach a large one.
JEV QUESTION
choice: small, medium or large LLM
LIVE DEMO
Model router by @ephraimduncan →
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Example prompts are illustrative.
Scenario 2 of 9
Guardrails
Check every input for injection, abuse or off-policy content before it reaches the LLM, and block whatever fails.
JEV QUESTION
noul: is this input safe to send?
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Example inputs are illustrative.
Scenario 3 of 9
Tool-call gating
When an agent wants to call a tool, Jev classifies the call: run it, ask the user first, or refuse.
JEV QUESTION
choice: allow, ask or deny
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Example tool calls are illustrative.
Scenario 4 of 9
Inbox triage
Sort a flood of email into what needs a reply now, what can wait, and what to archive.
JEV QUESTION
choice: reply now, later or archive
LIVE DEMO
500 emails for 3.5 cents, @rileybrown →
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Example emails are illustrative.
Scenario 5 of 9
Reranking
Given a query and a set of passages, Jev scores each one for relevance so you keep the best.
JEV QUESTION
score: how relevant is this passage to the query?
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Scores are the infographic’s; passages are illustrative.
Scenario 6 of 9
LLM evals
Have Jev grade another model’s output on a fixed scale, quickly and at low cost.
JEV QUESTION
score: how good is this answer, from 1 to 5?
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Example answers and scores are illustrative.
Scenario 7 of 9
Bulk labeling
Apply the same decision to every row of a huge table, map-reduce style, and get a label for each.
JEV QUESTION
choice: which label fits this row?
LIVE DEMO
Slop detector by @RBilgil →
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Labels A, B and C are placeholders.
Scenario 8 of 9
Real-time control
In a loop that runs every 300 ms, Jev reads the current state and picks the next action.
JEV QUESTION
choice: which action comes next?
LIVE DEMO
jev-trader by @jarrodwatts →
Jev plays Doom, @CompleteSkeptic →
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. The demo is slowed down; actions jump, duck and dodge are illustrative.
Scenario 9 of 9
Confidence gate
Act automatically when confidence is high, confirm when it is middling, and hand off to a human when it is low.
JEV QUESTION
any question, read with its confidence value
Source: ByteByteGo, “Top 9 places to use Jev”. Thresholds are the infographic’s examples.
